proof:
# A common residual simplex controls every parallel section

This is an arbitrary-dimensional geometric lemma. It uses one common
convex hull of actual points, rather than adding overlapping swept sets.

## 1. Actual residual regions and conclusion

Let d>=2, m=d+1, and let v_0,...,v_d span R^d with sole dependence
sum_i v_i=0. Let

    T={x:v_i.x<=1 for all i}

be a bounded full-dimensional simplex. Let A,B,K be d-dimensional
convex bodies with B subset T and (A+B)/2 subset K. Write b=vol_d(B).
For each j put

    R_j=A intersect intersection_(i!=j){x:v_i.x<-1}.

Let J be a set of k distinct indices, 2<=k<=m, for which every R_j
has positive d-volume. Choose an actual point P_j in each R_j and put

    P=conv{P_j:j in J},             r=k-1.

Then P is an r-dimensional simplex and

    vol_d(P+B)>2^r b.                                  (1)

Every normal indexed outside J is strictly missed on(P+B)/2. Thus

    vol_d(K intersect intersection_(i notin J){x:v_i.x<0})
                    > b/2^(d-k+1).                    (2)

When J contains all m indices, the intersection in(2) is interpreted
as the whole K. In that case additionally vol_d(A)>vol_d(T)>=b.
Criticality and equality of cap masses are not assumptions of this lemma.

## 2. An elementary positive inverse

Use the affine coordinates

    lambda_i(x)=(1+v_i.x)/m,         sum_i lambda_i(x)=1.

The map x->lambda(x) is an affine isomorphism from R^d to the
coordinate hyperplane of sum1. The simplex -T is lambda_i>=0 for all i,
whereas T is lambda_i<=2/m for all i.

Let C be the m by k matrix whose j-th column is lambda(P_j). Since
P_j belongs to R_j,

    C_jj>1,        C_ij<0 for i!=j,
    sum_i C_ij=1.                                    (3)

Let C_J denote the square submatrix with rows indexed by J. Its
column sums are at least1 (strictly greater than1 if k<m), because
the omitted entries are negative. Write C_J=D-N, with D its positive
diagonal and N having zero diagonal and nonnegative off-diagonal entries.
For each column,

    sum_i (N D^(-1))_ij <1.

Consequently its induced column-sum norm is less than1, and the
geometric matrix series converges absolutely:

    C_J^(-1)=D^(-1) sum_(q>=0)(N D^(-1))^q >=0.        (4)

This proves invertibility and positivity without invoking an unproved
matrix theorem. Invertibility implies affine independence of the P_j:
an affine dependence of them would give a vector in the kernel of C_J.
Thus P has exactly dimension r=k-1.

## 3. Every parallel T section fits inside a reflected copy of P

Let F be the linear space parallel to aff(P), and take any affine
translate z+F having nonempty intersection with T. Its points may be
written in lambda coordinates as

    lambda(x)=c+C theta,        sum_j theta_j=1,
    sum_i c_i=0,                                      (5)

for one fixed vector c. For example, choose one point z_0 in that
affine plane and put c=lambda(z_0)-lambda(P_j0); then translate the
affine parametrization of P by z_0-P_j0. The parameter map is an
affine isomorphism onto the section plane, by the independence above.

Membership in T is equivalent to

    C theta<=h,       h_i=2/m-c_i,       sum_i h_i=2.

Define

    M=C_J^(-1)h_J,                U=sum_j M_j.

By(4), every feasible theta satisfies theta<=M. Hence U>=1. For
rows outside J all entries of C are negative, so theta<=M implies

    h_out>=C_out theta>=C_out M.

Summing these inequalities together with C_J M=h_J and using the
column sums in(3) gives

    2=sum_i h_i >=sum_i(CM)_i=sum_j M_j=U.

Thus1<=U<=2, and every section parameter belongs to

    Q={theta:theta<=M, sum theta=1}
      =M-(U-1)Delta,

where Delta is the standard simplex of nonnegative coordinates of sum1.
In physical space this is a translate of -(U-1)P. In particular every
parallel section is contained in a translate of -sP for some0<=s<=1.

Its r-volume is in fact strictly smaller than that of P. If U=1,
the section is a point and r>=1. If U>1, every vertex

    theta^(j)=M-(U-1)e_j

of Q violates a T inequality: choose any i in J distinct from j;
by(3),

    (C_J theta^(j))_i=h_i-(U-1)C_ij>h_i.

Hence the compact section is a proper closed convex subset of the
r-dimensional containing simplex Q and omits a neighborhood of a
vertex inside Q. Such a neighborhood has positive r-volume. Therefore

    vol_r(T intersect (z+F))
       <(U-1)^r vol_r(P)<=vol_r(P),                  (6)

unless the section is lower-dimensional, in which case the same final
strict bound holds because vol_r(P)>0. Volumes here are the standard
Euclidean measures on the parallel r-planes; their affine parametrizations
have the same Jacobian, so no untracked coordinate factor enters(6).

## 4. One Minkowski sum and sectionwise volume growth

Disintegrate d-volume using orthogonal projection onto F perpendicular.
Let B_y be the r-section of B over transverse coordinate y. It is a
convex subset of the corresponding T section, so by(6)

    vol_r(B_y)<vol_r(P)

at every nonempty section. The simplex P has one fixed transverse
coordinate y_P, and

    (P+B)_(y+y_P)=P+B_y.

This is equality of the actual sections of one Minkowski sum. For each
B_y of positive r-volume, the r-dimensional Brunn--Minkowski inequality
gives

    vol_r(P+B_y)^(1/r)
       >=vol_r(P)^(1/r)+vol_r(B_y)^(1/r)
       >2 vol_r(B_y)^(1/r).

Integrating yields(1), with strictness because the positive-volume
sections have positive total integral b>0. Null sections do not affect
the argument. When r=d, the same argument is simply the ordinary
d-dimensional Brunn--Minkowski inequality, without a transverse integral.

For every i outside J all chosen P_j have v_i.P_j<-1. Their finite
convex hull therefore satisfies the same strict inequality, and adding
B subset {v_i.x<=1} gives

    (P+B)/2 subset K intersect intersection_(i notin J){v_i.x<0}.

The common dilation by1/2 scales d-volume by2^(-d). This proves(2).
If k=m, equation(6) applied to the entire T gives vol_d(P)>vol_d(T);
since P subset A, the additional volume conclusion follows.

## 5. Full residual coverage gives a strict critical-cap depth margin

When J contains all m indices, the proof gives the stronger set inclusion

    -T subset P subset A.                            (7)

Indeed C is now square and has column sums1, so
1^T C^(-1)=1^T. For every lambda in the standard coordinate simplex,
theta=C^(-1)lambda is nonnegative by(4) and has coordinate sum1.
Thus lambda is a convex combination of the columns of C. Since -T
is exactly lambda_i>=0, this proves(7).

For this full containment assertion, strict residual points are not
needed. Define the closed corner regions

    C_j=A intersect intersection_(i!=j){v_i.x<=-1}.

If all m of them are nonempty, choose one actual P_j in each. Their
matrix now has C_jj>=1 and C_ij<=0 for i!=j, still with every column
sum equal to1. Its diagonal exceeds the sum of the absolute values of
the off-diagonal entries in its column by exactly1. The same convergent
matrix series in(4) gives C^(-1)>=0, even if some off-diagonal entries
vanish. The column-sum argument above again proves -T subset conv(P_j)
subset A. No strict volume or strict section-containment assertion is
inferred for this closed-corner extension; only(7) is needed below.

Here is a concrete mixed-fiber consequence with all assumptions stated.
Work with exactly

    S=({-1} times A) union ({0} times K) union ({1} times B),

with full d-dimensional fibers as above and0 in the interior of K.
Let Q be its genuine raw halfspace depth at(0,0), and suppose every
ambient cap

    H_i={(z,x):v_i.x>=z},           i=0,...,d,

attains Q. All A cuts are proper and every B capture is zero-volume.
Assume all m actual closed corner regions C_j are nonempty. This
includes, but does not require, positive-volume strict residual regions.
Put Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d and M=a+k+b.
Then

    Q/M>3Gamma/5>Gamma/2.                            (8)

To prove this, write U_i for each captured A volume and q_i for the
middle captured volume. Since there are exactly three fibers,

    Q=U_i+q_i.

Set inclusion(7) implies U_i>=V>=b: every A cap v_i.x>=-1 contains
the whole -T, whose volume is V.

For clarity, the exact tilt-equalization input is proved here. Vary the
ambient cap to v_i.x>=theta z, keeping the source and its middle trace
fixed. The endpoint captured volumes vary continuously with theta; their
difference tends to -b as theta tends to negative infinity and to a as
theta tends to positive infinity. At a finite theta they are equal to
some t. Genuine source criticality gives U_i<=2t. Since U_i>=b>0,
we have t>0, so both endpoint caps have positive volume. Their midpoint
sum lies in the fixed middle cap. Brunn--Minkowski therefore gives
q_i>=t. Consequently

    U_i<=2q_i,             U_i<=2Q/3.                (9)

This verifies the tilt-equalization hypothesis using actual containing
ambient halfspaces; it does not round or average the source point.

The caps v_i.x>=-1 cover A, and the middle traces v_i.x>=0 cover K.
Apply the ordinary Grunbaum inequality to each body's centroid and to
one covering cap containing that centroid. Their cap upper bounds give

    Gamma a<=2Q/3,
    Gamma k<=Q-b.                                    (10)

The second inequality retains the common lower bound U_i>=b in
q_i=Q-U_i. Summing(10) with the B volume,

    M<=5Q/(3Gamma)-(1-Gamma)b/Gamma
      <5Q/(3Gamma).

Since d>=2, 0<Gamma<1 and b>0, the last inequality is strict. This
proves(8). In particular any source in this exact critical-circuit
regime whose depth is at most Gamma M/2 must have at least one actual
CLOSED corner region C_j empty. The strict-separation part of
`candidate 2adcc478e651c9c4`
therefore supplies an averaged normal with min_A u>-1 for at least
one index. This is a proved structural restriction, not an assumption
that the remaining residual patterns cannot occur.

## Scope

The points P_j are deterministic actual points of the same A, and
their whole convex hull remains in A. The positive residual-volume
assumptions are explicit; this note does not assert that every critical
cap family has such a collection of residual regions. Formula(2) is
a joint missed-region lower bound, not an OC centerpoint theorem.
The pair case k=2 recovers the coarser strict bound in
`candidate bad2020086fc16b6`.
The direction-specific simplex chord estimate can sharpen that pair
case further, but no sum of the overlapping pairwise swept sets is
used or inferred here.
